focus: Local staging, tiling, reuse, and load-compute-store. Keep compute off m_axi.
merge_rule: Union of the 90-skill package and gemm_flatten_v2. On id conflicts, gemm_flatten_v2 replaces the 90-skill entry.

guards: do not tile only because an array is large
do not apply tiling if each element is streamed once with no reuse or scheduling benefit
do not simply copy data into a local buffer while leaving scalar compute unchanged
do not allocate dynamic or excessively large tile buffers
preserve boundary conditions and numerical behavior
skills.pattern: a loop nest repeatedly accesses a bounded region of a large array, matrix, grid, or neighbor window from global memory, and this region can be staged locally to enable reuse, pipelining, unrolling, or local-buffer partitioning
required_steps: identify the reused or repeatedly accessed global-memory region
choose compile-time tile dimensions that fit local memory
rewrite outer loops to iterate over tile blocks
load the tile with pipelined unit-stride accesses
rewrite compute indexing from global references to local tile-buffer references
reuse local tile values or exploit local tile bandwidth for parallel computation
pipeline the tile compute loop
unroll independent inner loops when local memory bandwidth can support it
partition or bank local buffers to match unroll factor
handle tails, boundaries, and halo regions safely
store only valid output elements
skills.strategy: do not tile only because the array is large; reshape the loop nest around tiles, stage the reusable working set into local memory, rewrite compute indexing to use local tile coordinates, and exploit the local tile through pipelining, inner-loop unrolling, and buffer partitioning when legal

guards: do not tile only because the array is large
do not tile pure streaming loops with no reuse or scheduling benefit
do not copy into a local buffer while leaving the computation effectively scalar and unchanged
do not allocate dynamic or excessive local buffers
validate that tiling improves II, latency, memory traffic, or enables local parallelism
skills.pattern: a one-dimensional loop or flattened array traversal repeatedly accesses a bounded contiguous region from global memory, and this working set can be staged locally to enable reuse, pipelining, unrolling, or local-buffer partitioning
required_steps: identify the reused or repeatedly accessed 1D global-memory region
choose a compile-time TILE size that fits BRAM/URAM/LUTRAM
rewrite the outer loop to advance by TILE
load each tile into a local buffer with pipelined unit-stride accesses
rewrite compute from in[global_index] to tile[local_index] where legal
pipeline the tile compute loop
unroll independent local-index or lane loops when useful
partition or bank local buffers to support the unrolled compute
handle N not divisible by TILE
store only valid output elements
skills.strategy: strip-mine the 1D iteration space into tiles, stage each tile into local memory, rewrite compute indexing from global indices to local tile indices, reuse tile data or exploit local tile bandwidth, and expose parallelism through pipelining, lane/inner-loop unrolling, and buffer partitioning when legal

guards: do not ignore top, bottom, left, or right boundaries
do not compute halo-only elements as valid outputs unless the original algorithm does so
ensure tile plus halo fits local memory
avoid changing numerical behavior at grid borders
handle partial tiles at matrix/image edges
skills.pattern: the computation operates on a 2D grid, matrix, image, or dynamic-programming table where each output depends on nearby elements that are reused across neighboring iterations
required_steps: identify TILE_R and TILE_C
identify halo radius in rows and columns
allocate a local tile buffer including halo
load tile interior and halo safely
rewrite global neighbor accesses to local tile-buffer accesses
compute only valid output points for the tile
pipeline row/column compute loops
unroll an independent inner dimension if local buffer banking supports it
partition or bank local tile buffers when needed
preserve original boundary behavior
skills.strategy: tile the 2D iteration space, load the tile plus halo/border region into local memory, rewrite neighbor accesses from global coordinates to local tile coordinates, and pipeline/unroll computation over the valid tile interior

guards: do not stage unbounded or runtime-sized arrays entirely on-chip
do not skip local staging because m_axi pragmas are already present
do not apply advanced optimizations on top of a reference port that still reads globals in compute
skills.pattern: kernel has m_axi or global array arguments and the hot loop reads or writes those arrays directly
required_steps: identify all array parameters accessed in the hot loop
estimate compile-time working-set size (inputs + outputs + temporaries)
if working set fits on-chip BRAM budget, stage full arrays locally in one load pass
else choose tiling with reuse analysis, not a default small tile size
add #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 to every dedicated load and store loop
add #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 to the local-memory compute loop when legal
verify compute indexing uses local buffers, not global array parameters
before submitting, confirm the kernel body contains PIPELINE pragmas on every major compute phase; zero PIPELINE on compute is a blocking defect
only after this baseline is in place, apply advanced skills (tiling, unroll, coalescing)
skills.strategy: before any tiling, unrolling, coalescing, or DATAFLOW: separate into bulk load, pipelined local compute, and bulk store; never leave the hot compute loop on global or m_axi memory

guards: do not change top-level pointer element types unless explicitly allowed
pair with distinct gmemN bundles per port when parallelizing external access
local arrays must be sized with fixed bounds from header macros
skills.pattern: kernel touches m_axi pointer ports in compute loops and may benefit from pipelining, unroll, or DATAFLOW but must not bottleneck on repeated external memory RMW
required_steps: identify every m_axi port used in compute
add local buffers for reused arrays and private scalar accumulators for reductions
pipeline load, compute, and store loops independently where legal
write each output m_axi element at most once per logical update (after local finalize)
apply tiling when full arrays exceed on-chip budget while keeping RMW off m_axi inside inner loops
skills.strategy: Use explicit load-compute-store: (1) load required inputs from m_axi into local on-chip buffers or private scalars; (2) perform all repeated updates, reductions, and accumulations on locals only; (3) store final results back to m_axi outputs once per element when possible. Prefer burst-friendly sequential loads/stores and separate phases.

skills.pattern: pipelined load_tile, compute_tile, or store_tile loops use for (i = 0; i < tile_size; i++) where tile_size is runtime-computed for the final partial tile
skills.strategy: Loop bound must be compile-time TILE_SIZE from header macros; use if (tile_i + i < N) guards for partial final tile. Runtime tile_size as loop bound blocks II=1 pipeline, UNROLL, and LOOP_FLATTEN (HLS 200-936/960).
required_steps: replace for (i = 0; i < tile_size; i++) with for (i = 0; i < TILE_SIZE; i++)
guard loads, stores, and compute with if (tile_i + i < N) or if (i < tile_size) only inside body — not as loop bound
keep tile_size scalar for guard comparisons when needed, not as pipelined loop trip count
re-apply PIPELINE II=1 on inner fixed-bound loops after rewrite
validate csynth no longer warns cannot unroll/flatten due to variable tile_size bound
guards: TILE_SIZE macro must match tiling pragma and local buffer allocation
preserve semantics for partial tail tile — skipped iterations must not change results
complements hls-rewrite-variable-trip-fixed-bound-guard for triangular inner bounds
do not allocate local arrays larger than synthesis can map
if full staging does not fit, increase tile size based on reuse and BRAM, not a fixed small constant
skills.pattern: compile-time array dimensions are bounded and total working set (all inputs, outputs, and needed temporaries) fits available on-chip memory without tiling
required_steps: sum element counts times sizeof for each array needed during compute
compare against conservative BRAM budget for the target FPGA
if it fits, allocate local arrays matching problem dimensions and use bulk load, compute, and store
choose tiling only when full staging exceeds on-chip budget or reuse analysis proves larger tiles are better
after full staging, apply hls-gemm-static-nest-flatten-and-k-partition (or equivalent) to every static GEMM nest
skills.strategy: load the full working set into local arrays once, run all compute on local memory, store once; do not default to nested small-tile loops that repeatedly reload the same global data. After staging, GEMM/matmul compute nests must still be flattened with k-dim partition — staging alone does not fix outer-i sequential latency.

guards: do not pipeline a loop that still performs multiple global neighbor reads per iteration
PIPELINE on global stencil loops without local staging will not achieve II=1
skills.pattern: inner loop body reads multiple offsets from the same array (neighbors, halos, diagonal or window indices, or index pairs from different dimensions) and those reads currently target global or m_axi memory
required_steps: count distinct offset reads per loop iteration
if more than one global read per iteration, local staging is required
choose line buffer or sliding window for streaming neighbor patterns, or tile blocking for random multi-index updates
pipeline traversal over local data with II=1 when legal
skills.strategy: stage the accessed region into local buffers, line buffers, sliding windows, or tiles so all neighbor reads in the hot loop come from on-chip memory; route to ii-stencil-linebuffer-window-shift or tiling skills as appropriate

guards: do not perform global load/store inside the time-step loop when the full volume fits on-chip
use old/new local volumes or planes rather than per-tile global round-trips each timestep
hardcoding trip counts instead of using compile-time constants is a separate defect
skills.pattern: an outer time-step or iteration loop performs a 2D or 3D neighbor stencil that reads and writes grid values, and the current code accesses global or m_axi arrays inside the time-step loop
required_steps: load the full grid or each needed volume into local memory once before the time-step loop
allocate two local buffers for old/new state when the stencil alternates between two arrays
perform all neighbor reads from local buffers inside the time-step loop
pipeline the innermost legal traversal loop with II=1
swap or copy old/new buffers between time steps without global round-trips
store the final volume once after all time steps
skills.strategy: for iterative stencils, keep the working volume on-chip across time steps using full-grid local buffers or old/new planes; never leave the time-step loop on global memory

guards: do not ignore boundary conditions or halo behavior
window update order must preserve old neighbor values before shifting
ensure line-buffer depth matches image/grid width or tile width
if the stencil has true time-step dependencies, use old/new buffers or wavefront scheduling as needed
skills.pattern: a 1D/2D stencil, convolution, image, grid, or neighbor-access loop repeatedly reads adjacent elements from global or local memory, causing port conflicts, redundant loads, or loop-carried neighbor dependencies
required_steps: identify stencil radius and neighbor access pattern
create line buffers for previous rows or shift registers for previous columns/elements
create a small fully partitioned compute window
stream new input values through the line buffer/window update each cycle
rewrite neighbor references to window entries
pipeline the main traversal loop with II=1 when legal
handle warm-up, borders, halos, and partial tiles explicitly
skills.strategy: replace repeated neighbor reads with line buffers and a sliding window/shift register; load one new element per cycle, shift local window state, compute from the partitioned window, and write valid outputs after boundary guards

guards: do not spill an intermediate consumed by the next phase if it fits in on-chip memory
preserve producer-consumer ordering between phases
only write final outputs or arrays not reused later to global memory
skills.pattern: the kernel has multiple dependent compute phases where an intermediate array produced in one phase is consumed by a later phase, and the current design writes that intermediate to global memory between phases
required_steps: identify arrays written in one phase and read in a later phase
allocate local buffers for each reused intermediate result
run phase 1 compute into local intermediate buffers
run later phases using only local intermediates
partition or bank local buffers to match inner-loop unroll factor
store only final outputs that are not consumed again
pipeline load, each local phase, and final store
for matrix-multiply phases, flatten (i,j) and partition on k; do not leave sibling phases with mismatched flatten
skills.strategy: keep every intermediate result that is consumed by a later phase in on-chip local memory; chain phases locally and defer global writes until the value is no longer needed

guards: apply even when the temporary array is also an m_axi output port
preserve the external ABI by storing the local temporary once after all consuming phases complete
reject a phase whose csynth loop table shows compute_* outer trip=M, II=-, Pipelined=no while an inner j claims II=1
if one GEMM phase flattened and a sibling did not, copy the successful partition+flatten pattern onto the slow phase
skills.pattern: the kernel chains two or more matrix multiplies or GEMM-like phases where a temporary array is written in one phase and read in the next phase, and the temporary is currently written to global memory between phases
required_steps: identify the temporary array produced by phase 1 and consumed by phase 2
allocate a local buffer for the temporary with the same compile-time dimensions
partition A/B/tmp/C locals on the k (reduction) access dimension — required when k is fully unrolled
run each GEMM phase with PIPELINE II=1 on (i,j), UNROLL on k, and LOOP_FLATTEN (or a single ij loop)
verify each phase reports one flattened pipeline over ~M*N trips, not sequential outer i
if phase2 flattened and phase1 did not, mirror phase2's partition+flatten onto phase1
store the temporary to its global port only once if the ABI requires it
skills.strategy: never chain GEMM phases through global memory; keep the temporary in a local buffer across phases and pipeline both multiplies on-chip. For each GEMM phase with static bounds: partition locals on the reduction (k) dimension, PIPELINE II=1 the (i,j) nest with k fully unrolled, and require nest flatten so outer i is not left sequential.

guards: on-chip BRAM budget may require tiling — reuse tiles, not duplicate full matrices
preserve numerical semantics when reordering multiply-add chains
do not add decorative multi-task DATAFLOW without streams — see avoid-dataflow-without-stream-or-overlap-proof
skills.pattern: chained matrix multiplies (output = alpha * A*B + beta * … with multiple GEMM stages) implemented with multiple full-size local temporaries and extra copy loops between stages
required_steps: identify GEMM chain depth and which intermediates must persist vs can be streamed
allocate the smallest local buffers that cover one tile or one K-panel, not full N×N per stage
pipeline innermost K loop with II=1; partition locals on K/column dim to match unroll
remove redundant matrix-to-matrix copy loops between DATAFLOW tasks

if one local buffer (e.g. tmp) is consumed by two downstream tasks (second GEMM + store), insert hls::stream or duplicate buffer with single-writer/single-reader chain — never one writer + two concurrent readers (HLS 200-779)
add DATAFLOW between GEMM stages only with hls::stream panel FIFOs and overlap report
fold alpha/beta scaling into the same local accumulator where numerically legal
skills.strategy: Reuse minimal local tile or K-panel accumulators; pipeline the K dimension innermost with ARRAY_PARTITION on the K access dimension; avoid allocating local_tmp1/local_tmp2/local_tmp3 full-matrix buffers and copy tasks between GEMM stages. Prefer one compute nest per tile or stream K-panels between stages via hls::stream when DATAFLOW overlap is real.

guards: on-chip BRAM budget must fit both layouts or tile the shared load
transposed layout indexing must match compute access pattern
const m_axi inputs: one read per element per logical load pass
skills.pattern: algorithm needs both row-major and column-oriented (transposed) local views of the same matrix for matrix-vector or multi-phase compute
required_steps: identify phases that need A[i][j] and A[j][i] or column-slice vs row-slice access
single pipelined load loop: read A[i][j] from m_axi once per element
write the value into row-major local_A[i][j] and transposed local_AT[j][i] in the same iteration
run compute from locals only — no second full-matrix m_axi load
store outputs once after local finalize
skills.strategy: Load the matrix from m_axi once and populate both normal and transposed local buffers from the same external read stream. Do not read the full matrix twice from m_axi unless explicitly required by correctness.

guards: statistics vectors such as mean and stddev should also be computed and stored locally when small
preserve numerical semantics of each pass
pipeline each pass separately; do not reread the full dataset from global memory every pass if it fits locally
skills.pattern: the kernel performs multiple passes over the same dataset (reduction, normalization, pairwise aggregation, correlation, covariance, or similar) with repeated global reads and writes of the main data array between passes
required_steps: identify all passes that traverse the same main data array
if the dataset fits on-chip, load it into a local buffer once
compute mean, variance, normalization, and aggregation passes over the local buffer with pipelined loops
keep small statistic vectors in local memory
write normalized data and final output matrix back in dedicated store loops
avoid leaving hot passes as unpipelined scalar loops on global memory
skills.strategy: stage the main data array locally, run every statistics or normalization pass on local memory with pipelined loops, and minimize repeated global traversals of the same array

guards: do not stage unbounded data into local memory
do not add local buffering if each element is used once and no scheduling benefit appears
preserve output order and boundary behavior
combine with coalescing for contiguous global loads/stores when appropriate
skills.pattern: a pipeline-eligible loop directly accesses AXI/global memory, causing high II, unstable scheduling, or repeated memory latency, and the data can be staged into a bounded local buffer
required_steps: identify global-memory accesses inside the target compute loop
separate load, compute, and store phases when legal
stage a bounded region into a local buffer
pipeline the local compute loop
partition local buffers if multiple local accesses per cycle are needed
store results back with a pipelined loop
handle tails and boundaries safely
skills.strategy: separate global-memory load/store from compute, stage data into local buffers with pipelined burst-friendly loops, and pipeline the compute loop over local memory; combine with tiling, coalescing, or partitioning when the access pattern supports it

guards: avoid complete partitioning of large 2D tiles
partition the dimension that corresponds to parallel accesses
do not partition if it does not address the actual port conflict
skills.pattern: tiled compute introduces parallel local-buffer accesses, but the local tile buffer has insufficient memory ports to support pipelining or unrolling
required_steps: identify which local buffer dimension is accessed in parallel
match cyclic or complete partitioning to the unroll factor
prefer complete partition for small lane buffers
prefer cyclic partition for larger regularly indexed tile buffers
inspect II and local memory resource usage after partitioning
skills.strategy: partition or bank local tile buffers along the dimension accessed in parallel, matching the partition factor to the unroll factor or access pattern

guards: m_axi pragmas on many ports do not remove the need for local staging
each phase still needs pipelined loops over local data
do not leave any phase as a scalar nest on global arrays
skills.pattern: the kernel contains multiple sequential loop nests or update phases over matrices and vectors exposed as m_axi arguments, and one or more phases still read or write those arguments directly in the hot loops
required_steps: list all phases and the arrays each phase reads or writes
load every array touched by more than one phase into local buffers once
rewrite each phase to use only local buffers with pipelined loops
apply hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally when later phases consume earlier outputs
store only final results that must be visible off-chip
add array_partition on local arrays accessed in parallel inner loops
for each GEMM-like phase, require flatten of (i,j) and k-dim partition; fail the design if any phase keeps outer i sequential
skills.strategy: for multi-phase kernels, bulk-load shared inputs to locals, execute every phase as pipelined local-memory compute with flattened static nests where applicable, and bulk-store final outputs once; never emit a reference-style multi-loop port on global memory.

guards: do not stage unbounded data into local memory
do not add local buffering if each element is used once and no scheduling benefit appears
preserve output order and boundary behavior
handle tails safely
skills.pattern: a loop is pipeline-eligible, but direct global-memory access through m_axi prevents low II or stable scheduling
required_steps: identify global-memory accesses inside the target compute loop
separate load, compute, and store phases when legal
load a bounded region into a local buffer
pipeline the local compute loop
store results back with a pipelined loop
combine with coalescing or tiling when access pattern supports it
skills.strategy: separate global-memory load/store from compute, stage data into local buffers with pipelined burst-friendly loops, and pipeline the compute loop over local memory

skills.pattern: triangular or variable-bound loops such as for (k=0; k<i), for (k=0; k<j), for (j=i+1; j<N), or for (i=0; i<tile_size) blocking II=1 pipeline
skills.strategy: Rewrite to fixed compile-time bounds (N, TILE_SIZE from header macros) and preserve semantics with if guards on the induction variable.
required_steps: replace runtime or outer-dependent bounds with fixed TILE_SIZE or N
wrap body in if (idx < original_bound) to skip out-of-range iterations
apply PIPELINE II=1 only on the fixed-bound inner loop after rewrite
keep tile_size as a scalar for guard comparisons, not as the loop bound when pipelining
guards: do not change numerical results — guards must match original iteration set
prefer TILE_SIZE macro over function parameter for synthesizable bounds
each bundle still needs burst-friendly access patterns on its port
do not duplicate bundle names across unrelated ports
cosim and interface pragmas must stay consistent after rebundling
skills.pattern: kernel has two or more m_axi pointer ports and uses #pragma HLS DATAFLOW or multiple load/compute/store tasks that should overlap external memory access
required_steps: enumerate every m_axi port on the top kernel and on DATAFLOW subfunctions that touch global memory
assign each pointer port a unique bundle=gmemN (gmem0, gmem1, gmem2, …)
map load tasks to read ports and store tasks to write ports on separate bundles when stages overlap
re-run csynth and verify parallel tasks no longer stall on a single gmem port (HLS 200-885 on gmem)
pair with hls::stream or proven stage overlap — distinct bundles alone do not fix decorative DATAFLOW
skills.strategy: Assign a distinct bundle=gmem0, gmem1, … to each m_axi pointer port so HLS can issue concurrent external memory transactions across DATAFLOW stages. Never place all read/write ports on a single bundle=gmem when stages are meant to run concurrently.
skills.template:
// BAD: all ports share one bundle — DATAFLOW tasks serialize on gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem

// GOOD: one bundle per port for concurrent stage access
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem0
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem1
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem2

guards: do not interchange loops when it violates data dependencies or output order
manual loop interchange is not useful if the tool already performs it and no access pattern changes
after reordering, partition the dimension actually accessed in parallel
verify boundaries and row-major/column-major indexing carefully
skills.pattern: a loop nest misses II because the innermost pipelined loop uses strided/non-contiguous global accesses, repeatedly hits the same local memory bank, or places the dependency-carrying dimension in the hot pipeline
required_steps: identify current inner-loop memory stride and dependency direction
determine whether loop interchange or strip-mining preserves semantics
choose an inner dimension with contiguous global access or conflict-free bank mapping
update local buffer layout and ARRAY_PARTITION dim to match the new inner loop
rewrite index expressions and boundary/tail handling
pipeline the new hot loop and inspect burst/II reports
skills.strategy: reorder or strip-mine loops so the pipelined inner loop is unit-stride for global memory, maps parallel lanes to distinct local banks, or moves true dependencies to an outer sequential dimension when legal
